scope: Early traction for small consumer and prosumer software (solo or tiny team, little audience, little budget). Public sources only; a brand's own results stay in its private engine state, tagged with these ids.

tactics.tactic: Participate helpfully in communities where the audience already asks for help for weeks before sharing; follow each venue's self-promotion rule and ask moderators first.
tactics.fits: Pre-launch or pre-PMF, zero audience, zero budget.

cases.what: ~4 weeks of Reddit productivity participation and founder DMs before launch: '90% of the work is done in the four weeks before'
First users from contribute-first posts in remote-work Facebook groups and Reddit after asking admins

counterEvidence: Large problem communities (e.g. r/productivity, r/ADHD) ban promotion entirely; posting links there burns the account.

New or low-history accounts that post links to their own site are commonly caught by Reddit's spam filtering and can be shadowbanned site-wide; restrictions are lifted only by appeal (https://help.postpone.app/platforms/reddit/spam-suspensions-and-shadowbans).
tactics.transferLimits: Must be done as a real person, not automated. Traffic from no-link comments is near zero; the value is audience language and trust.

tactics.tactic: Personally watch or interview every early user, fix onboarding, and run the 'very disappointed' survey once ~40+ users are active.
tactics.fits: Any pre-PMF product with a handful of users.

cases.what: Surveyed 100–200 users; 'very disappointed' rose 22% → 58% by segmenting and fixing
Onboarding calls and session replays for a summer to fix activation

tactics.transferLimits: Retention work, not acquisition; needs analytics access and some users.

tactics.tactic: Pitch editors and newsletters that cover the category; localization or a seasonal angle can be the hook.
tactics.fits: Products with a clear, demonstrable angle.

cases.what: German localization led to German tech-blog coverage and a first App Store feature (>20k downloads that month)
Self-submitted to Lifehacker and Digg after a blog launch; ReadWriteWeb coverage followed

tactics.transferLimits: 2007-era blogs reached the whole market; today's equivalents are smaller niche newsletters.

tactics.tactic: Share the build, numbers and demos from the founder's own account.
tactics.fits: Founders willing to be visible; slow from zero followers.

cases.what: Own Twitter plus friends: >1,000 downloads in month one
Building in public on Twitter led to an investor acquisition and ~950 paying users

counterEvidence: Brand accounts with no followers get near-zero reach; reach for indie builders on X is lower than in 2020–21.
tactics.transferLimits: Requires a real person's identity; brands that keep the founder anonymous cannot use it.

tactics.tactic: Time launches and content to moments of category intent (New Year planning, back to school) and join indie promotions.

cases.what: >35k downloads in January 2021 from New Year's resolutions and Indie App Santa

tactics.transferLimits: Pages need weeks to be indexed before the season starts.

tactics.tactic: Ship a free, no-signup, single-purpose tool that people search for and that launch communities accept, and route its users into the product.
tactics.fits: Products whose core action can be demonstrated in one step.

cases.what: Free no-login AI task breakdown ('Magic ToDo'); searched by name ('break down tasks goblin'). Traffic estimate ~900K visits/month is unverified

counterEvidence: A tool that gives generic output for the user's input loses visitors; it must answer the actual input.
tactics.transferLimits: Value to the business depends on routing tool users into the product.

tactics.tactic: Dedicated pages for long-tail queries where small sites already rank (e.g. 'to do list no sign up', method names like '1-3-5 rule').
tactics.fits: Any product with a frictionless trial.

cases.what: Google results for 'to do list no sign up' include small sites (freetoolonline, projoodle, mediashower)

counterEvidence: New domains with no inbound links rank slowly; pages alone did not produce clicks for one brand (21 impressions, 0 clicks).
tactics.transferLimits: Needs inbound links (directories, launches) to start ranking.

tactics.tactic: List on free directories that rank for 'X alternative' searches (AlternativeTo, SaaSHub, Microlaunch, Uneed free queue).
tactics.fits: Any product; slow queues, so start early.

cases.what: Listings rank for long-tail 'alternative to' queries; new apps wait months in the free queue

counterEvidence: Several directories (BetaList, Futurepedia) are now paid only.
tactics.transferLimits: Small direct traffic; main value is inbound links and alternative-search presence.

tactics.tactic: Product Hunt / Show HN once there is a list or user base to amplify; lead with a behaviour or angle, not the category.
tactics.fits: After community, list or early users exist.

cases.what: Product Hunt with a 6k email list: ~1,000 signups, ~400 active
Show HN 'todo app for procrastinators' reached 103 points while generic todo apps got 1–3

counterEvidence: Product Hunt without an audience: reports of 400 signups and 1 payer, or top-50 with ~zero signups (https://www.indiehackers.com/post/why-product-hunt-launch-won-t-save-your-startup-0b511875f8).
tactics.transferLimits: One shot per product every ~6 months on Product Hunt.

tactics.tactic: Target App Store keywords, collect reviews and localize once a native app is live.
tactics.fits: Products with a released iOS/Android app.

cases.what: App Store featuring after localization; later App of the Day

tactics.transferLimits: Only once the app is released.
